title: Controlled remote viewing created by Ingo Swann and used by the military; stages 8 through 18 not taught to the public
summary: Lyn Buchanan tells of Controlled remote viewing created by Ingo Swann and used by the military; stages 8 through 18 not taught to the public, about military use "for all those years" to present at an unknown place, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote:

plain: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, told podcast host Jesse Michels about controlled remote viewing, a method that claims to let a trained person describe faraway places or hidden things using only the mind. He says it was created by a man named Ingo Swann, used by the military for years to gather intelligence, and is now used by businesses, while its higher stages, eight through eighteen, are not taught to the public.
